hints.S38_A1: Grandma still has her OLD PHOTO ALBUMS and wants to SHOW them to her grandchildren. Ask: which verb means she valued and kept them dearly? 'Destroyed', 'hid' and 'discarded' would leave her nothing to show.
hints.S38_A2: The children HAD NEVER SEEN A VILLAGE like that KAMPUNG, so the stories gripped them completely. Ask: which verb means to hold somebody's whole attention? 'Bored', 'frightened' and 'angered' are all sour reactions.
hints.S38_A3: BUT signals a contrast: her movements are slow, yet her MIND stays ALERT. Ask: which adjective matches 'alert'? 'Dim', 'confused' and 'slow' would repeat the weakness instead of contrasting with it.
hints.S38_A4: He spends hours SANDING it down and PAINTING it a new colour in the GARAGE. Ask: which verb means bringing something old back to its former good condition? 'Destroying' and 'ignoring' would undo all that work.
hints.S38_A5: The dash proves it: I REMEMBER EVERY DETAIL of those AFTERNOON VISITS. Ask: which adjective means loved and held dear in memory? 'Ordinary' and 'forgettable' contradict remembering every single detail.
hints.S38_B1: EVERY SUNDAY marks a habit, so the verb stays present. The subject is MY GRANDMOTHER - one person, not the whole family she feeds. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb or the -s form?
hints.S38_B2: WHENEVER WE VISITED is finished past time, repeated again and again. Ask: what is the past form of this irregular verb? Adding -ed would produce a word that does not exist in English.
hints.S38_B3: NOBODY CAN HOLD OUR ATTENTION THE WAY HE DOES - he beats everyone in his family, not just one rival. Ask: for a whole group, comparative or superlative? 'Good' changes shape completely, and 'most good' is never English.
hints.S38_B4: TASTIER already carries its own -er ending, so nothing may add a second comparison on top. Ask: which choice simply STRENGTHENS a comparative that is already formed? 'More tastier' doubles it, and 'as … as' would make them equal.
hints.S38_B5: ADVICE cannot be counted - you never say 'two advices'. Ask: which word partners an uncountable noun? 'Few', 'a few' and 'many' all need separate things you can number one by one.
hints.S38_B6: JUST sits in front of the gap, and Grandmother's kueh is measured against BENGAWAN SOLO's - equally good, neither better. Ask: which pair keeps two things level? 'More … than' would push one in front.
hints.S38_B7: The ROCKING CHAIR did not make itself - BY MY GRANDFATHER HIMSELF names the maker, and he did it long ago. Ask: which choice is passive and past? Passive = a form of 'be' + a past participle.
hints.S38_B8: TOLD THE CHILDREN = a reported order, and this one forbids something: hands off her SILVER BRACELET. Ask: after 'told' + person, which verb form follows? And where does a negative word sit - before that infinitive, or inside it?
hints.S38_C1: MY GRANDMOTHER is the one doing the WAKING, so the gap is the person who acts. Ask: does a subject slot take the acting pronoun, or the one that receives an action? A possessive would need a noun right after it.
hints.S38_C2: VISIT is a verb, and Grandmother receives that action - I am the one doing it. Ask: after a verb, do you use the acting pronoun or the receiving one? 'Visit she' is not English.
hints.S38_C3: GRANDFATHER IS EIGHTY-FOUR, and the gap is whoever TENDS that garden. Ask: does an action-doer slot take a subject pronoun, an object pronoun, or a possessive? A possessive would need a noun after it.
hints.S38_C4: MOTHER CALLS somebody, and that somebody is on the receiving end of the calling. Ask: after a verb, do you use a subject pronoun or an object pronoun? 'Calls he' is not English.
hints.S38_C5: A noun follows the gap: HANDS. Ask: can a subject or object pronoun sit directly in front of a noun, or must that slot hold a possessive? 'He hands' and 'him hands' are both nonsense.
hints.S38_C6: TOGETHER means both grandparents, and the gap is the pair who HAVE TAUGHT me about life. Ask: does an acting slot take a subject pronoun, or the object form? 'Them have taught' is not English.
hints.S38_C7: STORIES is a noun, and it comes straight after the gap. Ask: which pronoun form is allowed to own a noun - subject, object, or possessive? 'They stories' and 'them stories' are both wrong.
hints.S38_C8: WITH is a preposition, and a preposition always takes the receiving form of a pronoun. Ask: which pronoun follows a preposition - the acting one, or the one that receives? 'With they' is not English.
hints.S38_D1: MOVING SLOWLY AND TIRING EASILY, yet their MINDS AND HEARTS stay full. Ask: which box word describes a weak BODY in old age? A word about the mind would destroy the contrast the sentence is building.
hints.S38_D2: The dash lists it: LESSONS ABOUT PATIENCE, HARD WORK AND KINDNESS, and it CANNOT BE LEARNED FROM A TEXTBOOK. Ask: which box word names deep understanding earned by living? It is a noun - 'the ___ they share'.
hints.S38_D3: They talk ABOUT THE OLD DAYS and pass on A LIVING PIECE OF FAMILY HISTORY. Ask: which box word is the verb for fondly recalling the past aloud? A noun cannot follow 'when grandparents'.
hints.S38_D4: A CONNECTION TO THE PAST THAT SHAPES THEIR IDENTITY AND VALUES - and the word CULTURAL sits right in front of the gap. Ask: which box word names what earlier generations hand down to a child?
hints.S38_D5: These moments GROW RARER WITH EVERY PASSING YEAR, so families are urged to hold them dear. Ask: which box word is the verb meaning to treasure something deeply? It follows 'should', so it must be a plain verb.
hints.S38_E1: THEY'RE opens out into two words - try it: 'they are wonderful stories' about life BEFORE INDEPENDENCE. Does that read properly? Ask: which spelling shows the stories BELONG to the grandparents?
hints.S38_E2: LISTENED is an action verb, and the underlined word says HOW Grandpa listened. Ask: which ending must an adjective take before it is allowed to describe an action? Adjectives belong to nouns only.
hints.S38_E3: WOMANS is the trap: this noun never builds its plural with a plain -s. Ask: what do you call more than one man, or more than one child? The vowel inside the word changes instead of an ending being tacked on.
hints.S38_E4: THE GRANDCHILDREN is the subject - many of them, folding dumplings. Ask: does a plural subject take 'was', or its plural partner? Match the verb to the subject, not to 'Grandma' standing next to it.
hints.S38_E5: Count them: FOUR BROTHERS, not two. Ask: does a comparative or a superlative pick the top one out of a group of four? Uncle Rajan is being ranked against all of them at once.
hints.S38_F1: Which half is cause, and which is effect? FIFTY YEARS of gardening came first; knowing EVERY PLANT came afterwards. Ask: after 'Since', do you write the reason or the result? A comma then joins the halves.
hints.S38_F2: Find the noun both sentences share: GRANDMOTHER'S KUEH. Ask: must 'which' hug that noun, or trail at the very end? And what punctuation fences off the extra fact about FORTY YEARS of refining?
